_meta.purpose: Expected festival dates for src/astro_ai/festival_registry.py. Machine copy of the verified dataset; the registry is a hand transcription of the same data. scripts/verify_festivals.py diffs the two so a transcription slip cannot ship.
_meta.reckoning: purnimanta (North Indian) month naming. Diwali is purnimanta Kartika Amavasya = amanta Ashwina Amavasya — same night, two names.
_meta.source_secondary: independent Swiss Ephemeris tithi computation (pyswisseph 2.10.03, Lahiri sidereal, Delhi 28.6139N 77.2090E), checked against each festival's own observance window rather than sunrise alone
_meta.years_note: 2029 exists in the upstream verified dataset but is deliberately not listed here — the registry ships DATA_YEARS = (2026, 2027, 2028) and the hub's rolling 6-month window cannot reach 2029.
_meta.how_to_reverify: Open the source_urls year page on drikpanchang.com (New Delhi), read each festival's date off the published calendar, and cross-check the tithi with an ephemeris against that festival's own observance_window (moonrise for Karva Chauth, pradosh for Diwali, nishita for Shivratri/Janmashtami, madhyahna for Ram Navami/Ganesh Chaturthi, aparahna for Dussehra/Bhai Dooj) — not against sunrise. Then run scripts/verify_festivals.py.
_meta.to_add_a_year: Add the year to _meta.years, add its source URL to _meta.source_urls, add its adhik_maas windows (empty list if none), add the date to every festival's dates block, then add the same year to DATA_YEARS and every Festival.dates in festival_registry.py. Re-run scripts/verify_festivals.py — Gate 3 will refuse a whole-month error.
_meta.incident: Nine of the seventeen 2026 dates previously shipped in festivals.py were wrong by up to 21 days (Karva Chauth was 2026-11-05, Diwali 2026-11-08 — only 3 days apart when the tithi count demands 10-11). They were entered from memory under a header claiming a source it did not have. This file plus scripts/verify_festivals.py is the gate that stops that recurring.
_meta.caveat: Regional traditions legitimately observe some festivals on the adjacent day. Where the almanac splits (Ram Navami, Krishna Janmashtami) these are the Smarta / Drik dates.

adhik_maas._note: Intercalary lunar months (a lunar month containing no solar sankranti). Gate 2 skips cross-month tithi-interval invariants whose window an adhik maas falls inside; Gate 3 expects a +17..+21 day year-over-year jump across one. Computed from Swiss Ephemeris, confirmed against Drik for 2026.

holi.rule: day AFTER Phalguna Purnima (Holika Dahan is Purnima)

ram-navami.note: Smarta-tradition date. ISKCON may observe the following day (e.g. 2026-03-27). Drik flags 2028 explicitly as Smarta.

tithi_interval_invariants.why: Chaitra Shukla Navami -> Chaitra Purnima, 6 tithis apart in the same bright fortnight.
Shravana Purnima -> Bhadrapada Krishna Ashtami (purnimanta), 8 tithis.
Bhadrapada Krishna Ashtami -> Bhadrapada Shukla Chaturthi, 11 tithis across the same purnimanta month.
Ashwina Shukla Pratipada -> Ashwina Shukla Dashami, the nine nights.
Ashwina Shukla Dashami -> Kartika Krishna Chaturthi (purnimanta), 5 tithis to Purnima then 4.
Kartika Krishna Chaturthi -> Kartika Amavasya, 11 tithis. The 2026 bug had these 3 days apart.
Kartika Amavasya -> Kartika Shukla Pratipada, the next tithi.
Kartika Shukla Pratipada -> Kartika Shukla Dwitiya, the next tithi.
Kartika Shukla Dwitiya -> Kartika Shukla Ekadashi/Dwadashi.

drift_bands._note: Year-over-year movement of a tithi-based festival after normalising for Gregorian year length. A lunar year is ~11 days short of a solar one; a year in which an adhik maas intervenes runs ~19 days long instead.
